By using Claude.md and creating rules, sub-agents, and skills, and orchestrating security tool usage, we configure the agent for adversarial thinking, and perform research or attack/defense operations.

signals.brief_en:
Title: gadievron/raptor
Raptor repurposes Claude Code into a general‑purpose AI security agent capable of both offensive and defensive tasks. By leveraging Claude.md, defining rule‑sets, sub‑agents, and specialized skills, and orchestrating existing security tools, the system can adopt adversarial mindsets, conduct research, and execute attack or defence operations. The approach remains experimental; effectiveness depends on the quality of prompts, tool integration, and continuous oversight.

signals.title: @MarioNawfal: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman.
signals.content: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman. At least four vessels, including three U.S.-sanctioned tankers, have reportedly slowed down, circled cable routes and switched off their tracking systems at unusual moments. Maritime intelligence firm Windward says their movements are consistent with potentially mapping cable locations or placing explosives, although no sabotage has been confirmed. The activity follows explicit warnings from Iran's Revolutionary Guard that underwater internet cables, AI facilities and data centers could become targets if the U.S. and Israel launch another bombing campaign. The stakes are enormous. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar depend entirely on cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz for international internet connectivity. Damaging them could disrupt banking transactions, communications, cloud computing and digital businesses across the Gulf. With Washington continuing to move military assets toward the region, Tehran appears to be signaling that another war could threaten far more than oil shipments. Source: Financial Times / Writer: Mhedi
